question: In the shell-and-tube heat exchanger simulation with water (fine mesh), by what percentage did the heat transfer rate increase from 0.5 kg/s to 0.7 kg/s?
trap: the 35.64% the paper gives for the 1.25% nanofluid
rendered:
<document title="Heat Transfer Enhancement in a Shell-and-Tube Type of Heat Exchanger Using Al2O3/Water Nanofluid">
=== page 5 ===
- The most significant improvements are observed at a nanoparticle volume concentration of 1.25%, resulting in an average increase of 37.83% compared with pure water at the three different mass flow rates.
- For lower concentrations, the average increases in heat transfer are 7.16% at 0.25%, 15.47% at 0.50%, 23.32% at 0.75%, and 30.76% at 1.00%.
</document>

The percentage increase in heat transfer rate from 0.5 kg/s to 0.7 kg/s is 21.6% (21.6% = (114.98 - 94.43) / 94.43 * 100%).
